name: Eliakim
overview: Eliakim is a male descendant from the tribe of Judah, noted specifically as the son of Abihud within the Messianic lineage. His mention in Matthew 1:13 places him in the genealogical line leading to Jesus Christ, underscoring his role in the biblical ancestry of the Messiah. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliakim means 'G-d establishes,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning that emphasizes God's sovereign role in establishing his people. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a powerful connotation consistent with biblical themes of divine foundation and support.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Eliakim as the son of Abihud and the father of Azor, as explicitly stated in Matthew 1:13. These relationships situate him within a direct genealogical sequence that leads to Christ, highlighting his place in the ancestral line. Beyond these connections, no further family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Eliakim's significance lies primarily in his position within the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as recorded in Matthew 1:13. By being a link in the ancestral chain from Judah to the Messiah, he contributes to the fulfillment of Old Testament promises regarding the lineage of the Savior. His presence in this genealogy affirms the historical and theological continuity of God's redemptive plan through the tribe of Judah.
